[NFCT.6.2] **Per-fact accessors.** A `ds_fact_t *` is opaque; read it through:

| Accessor | Returns |
|---|---|
| `ds_fact_get_id`             | engine-assigned monotonic id (a new id after retract→reassert; identity is not preserved across retraction) |
| `ds_fact_get_schema`         | the schema this fact instantiates (borrow, engine-lifetime) |
| `ds_fact_get_asserted_ns`    | the fact's entry stamp, on the monotonic clock ([LTIM.2.8.6]) |
| `ds_fact_get_ttl_deadline_ns`| TTL deadline (0 for LOGICAL / untracked) |
| `ds_fact_get_slot_count`     | slot count |
| `ds_fact_get_slot`           | the i-th slot's name (borrow) and tagged-union value |

Each returns `DS_OK` with the out-pointer set, `DS_ERR_INVAL` on NULL,
`DS_ERR_NOT_FOUND` on out-of-range index. `ds_fact_get_slot` takes `NULL` for
either out-pointer, and `DS_ERR_INVAL` answers both being `NULL`. Pointers are
valid until the fact is retracted (TTL sweep, explicit retract, justifier-end);
holding a `ds_fact_t *` across pumps risks use-after-free unless you subscribe
to `DS_EV_FACT_RETRACT` and clear your reference there. A `v.json` read from a
fact is the fact's own tree, a borrow the caller must not free or change
([IDAT.3.3.8]).
